title: Complete EFX allocation of indivisible goods with additive values
aliases: envy-freeness up to the least positively valued good
decision_reason: Exact source-backed formulation, independent specialist status, current theorem-level scope checks, semantic distinctness and separated A25 self-review passed. Await batch refresh for active integration.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Complete partition of finitely many indivisible goods among finitely many agents; additive utilities.
problem_fingerprint.dimension: n agents and m goods, arbitrary finite sizes.
problem_fingerprint.domain: All profiles of nonnegative real item values.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Each v_i(S) is the sum of item values; zeros allowed; no common ordering, type, sparsity or bounded value-alphabet assumptions.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: No goods discarded, shared or fractionally assigned; empty bundles allowed.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every valuation profile, there exists one complete allocation satisfying every ordered-pair and every removed-good comparison.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: v_i(empty)=0 from additivity; no fixed total utility.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: v_i(A_i)>=v_i(A_j minus g) for all i,j and g in A_j, including zero-valued g.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Finite-instance exact existence, no asymptotic or probabilistic qualifier.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Universal existence of complete EFX0 allocations for additive goods.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Existence only; no runtime, Pareto optimality, welfare, payments or incentive constraints.

statement_source_and_scope_match: B25 §1 and definitions use nonnegative additive values, complete partition and every g in A_j. AFM26 §1 Definition 1 explicitly distinguishes EFX0 and positive-good EFX, and footnote 1 establishes equivalence of their universal existence questions; completeness and arbitrary nonnegative reals retained. Original CKM16 Definition 4.4 tests only positive goods, so zero-inclusive convention is attributed to modern restatements, not silently to the original.
proposed_statement_text: For every finite additive nonnegative goods instance there is a partition A with v_i(A_i)>=v_i(A_j minus g) for all i,j and every g in A_j.
applied_significance: Feasibility of a demanding fairness criterion for allocating indivisible assets/equipment under additive recipient preferences; differs from optimization of minimum utility.

source_records.title: Computing Envy-Free up to Any Good (EFX) Allocations via Local Search
source_records.supported_claim: Explicit open question for complete allocations and nonnegative additive values; local search is proved for identical strictly positive values, with broader experimental evidence.
source_records.access_limitations: Relevant definitions and theorem statements read; complete proof not independently verified.

source_records.access_limitations: Computer-assisted existence theorem reported; certificates were not independently executed.

hypothesis_comparison: All agents have the same strictly positive item values; broader profiles only tested experimentally.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Does not prove universal heterogeneous existence.

hypothesis_comparison: Four agents, at most nine goods; nonnegative real values, complete EFX0.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Arbitrary numbers of goods and agents remain outside this theorem.

hypothesis_comparison: Arbitrary population, at most three distinct additive valuation functions.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: General instances can have four or more distinct valuation functions.

hypothesis_comparison: Factor 2/3 for multigraph instances, n<=7, or a common three-value alphabet.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Factor multiplies the right-hand side; less than one does not imply EFX. Later exact multigraph result also remains restricted.

hypothesis_comparison: Disutilities; remove a chore from own bundle and compare remaining cost against another bundle.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Goods use nonnegative utility and removal from the envied bundle. Reversing utilities does not preserve these conditions.

hypothesis_comparison: Rank-based transformation has strictly diminishing marginals, rather than additive item values.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: The transformation does not preserve additivity; no additive counterexample follows.

hypothesis_comparison: Two distinct goods a,a_prime of type A satisfy u({a,a_prime})=u({a})=u({a_prime})>0.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Explicit violation of additivity excludes this instance from the candidate domain.

hypothesis_comparison: Each edge-good can be positively valued only by its endpoints.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: An unrestricted additive good may be valued by more than two agents.

hypothesis_comparison: For each agent, epistemic EFX permits a different repartition of the remaining goods as a certificate.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: No common actual partition satisfying all EFX comparisons is guaranteed. EFL itself still concerns the actual allocation.

hypothesis_comparison: PMMS implies EFX but EFX need not imply PMMS.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Failure of PMMS cannot establish failure of EFX; source explicitly preserves the EFX question.

hypothesis_comparison: Theorem 3 adds fractional Pareto optimality to additive EFX-or-MMS.
Theorem 4 yields EFX-or-MMS for an (n1,n2,1)-type instance.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Neither nonexistence theorem refutes unrestricted additive EFX, and the positive theorem does not establish it.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.difference: General Santa Claus optimizes minimum utility with an algorithmic approximation guarantee; EFX is exact pairwise envy relaxation feasibility.
Unrelated-machine makespan minimizes maximum load, not pairwise fairness of allocated utility.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: Retained all-320 inventory and baseline full-page review; repeated EFX, envy-freeness and PMMS text/alias screening; fully reread 289 and 290. No existing EFX entry.
implications_or_equivalences: Zero-inclusive and positive-good universal existence are counted once; positive perturbations and a finite allocation subsequence give the former from the latter.
Chores, partial allocations, algorithmic runtime, welfare and Pareto constraints are not additional variants counted here.

open_status_evidence_summary: Explicit formulation in CKM16 and B25; independent HV25, HT26 and September 2026 AZ26 retain additive-goods existence as open. Current full-text comparisons cover the apparent 2026 positive and negative results, including September 15 HKPV26.
independent_status_corroboration: B25, HV25, HT26 and AZ26 have mutually disjoint author groups and independently describe the remaining question. AFM26 corroborates exact finite scope but shares an author with several other partial-result sources, so those are not treated as independent of it.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Exact existence for at most three valuation types and, in the August preprint, four agents with at most nine goods; exact multigraph existence. AFR26 July revision reports unrestricted factor (sqrt(5)-1)/2. No universal exact additive-goods theorem or matching counterexample located.
